reason: E1 shows an MTP achieves ~4.6 meV/atom energy error for MoNbTaW, supporting near-DFT accuracy for a refractory HEA, but it does not address free energies, vibrational entropy, anharmonicity, or electron–vibration coupling. E2 is a CALPHAD study of Ta-Cr/V binaries and provides no evidence on MLIPs or free-energy methods. E3 reports DFT-computed vibrational entropy for CoCrFeNiTax but does not involve MLIPs or demonstrate that MLIPs can reproduce such entropies. Thus, the key premises about MLIPs capturing entropic contributions and reducing cost for fusion free-energy calculations are unsuppor
premises: Machine-learned interatomic potentials (MLIPs) can achieve near-DFT accuracy for energies and forces in refractory multicomponent alloys
Active learning can efficiently train MLIPs on a limited set of ab initio MD data
MLIPs can reproduce vibrational entropy and anharmonicity in solid and liquid phases
MLIPs can capture electron–vibration coupling effects
MLIP-based free-energy calculations are substantially cheaper than explicit ab initio MD or TOR-TILD for multicomponent systems
